source.title: Mitigating Overthinking in Large Reasoning Models via Manifold Steering
source.authors: Yao Huang; Huan-Ran Chen; Shou-Wei Ruan; Yi-Chi Zhang; Xing-Xing Wei; Yin-Peng Dong

record.tranche_reason: The paper applies a manifold-projected refusal direction and measures jailbreak success, testing refusal suppression with a modified intervention method.
record.gate_note: The refusal-feature experiment in Section 5.5 is relevant. The paper's overthinking-token and accuracy results concern a different behavior and are not included. Statements about prior refusal-ablation work are cited results, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: Section 5.5 re-runs difference-in-means refusal-direction ablation (data from Arditi et al.) on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. It reports AdvBench jailbreak success for the original-style direction and for a manifold-projected single direction. That bears on whether ablating one direction removes refusal (V1). The rest of the paper is about overthinking in reasoning models and is not relevant.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors report that manifold steering transfers to refusal-feature ablation (100% vs 74% AdvBench JSR) and call for stronger safety efforts.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the direction-computation data from [2], but applies the paper's manifold-projection method rather than testing only the original unprojected intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported baseline result is at α=2.0; the manifold-steering alpha for the 100% result is not stated. The paper compares baseline and manifold-steering methods.

fits_no_version.finding: Overthinking in R1-distilled reasoning models is captured by a diff-in-means direction whose ablation reduces tokens; the effect plateaus and rebounds at high α, fixed by manifold projection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Diff-in-means steering directions for other behaviours contain off-manifold noise that limits ablation strength.

record.problems: The refusal result is reported for one instruct model and one benchmark. The manifold-steering alpha is not stated, and the refusal experiment does not measure general capability preservation.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; preservation of general capabilities under refusal ablation (only a manual validity check of responses); other models and benchmarks.
No weight-edit or abliteration of released models.
No analysis of jailbreak mechanisms or adversarial training against ablation.
The manifold/PCA analysis is done for overthinking, not refusal; no multi-direction refusal test.
The refusal experiment uses a non-reasoning instruct model; the reasoning-model experiments concern overthinking only.

missing.what: JSR as a function of α (0.4 to 2.0) for baseline and manifold steering; the values are garbled in the text extraction, and the unablated JSR is not given.

record.verdict_notes: Refusal is a minor cross-task check in a paper about overthinking. There is one model and one benchmark, no uncertainty is reported, and no capability metric is given for the refusal setting. The α sweep in Figure 6 cannot be read from the extracted text.

versions.untested_parts: Tests only the harmful-request refusal-removal aspect, using a manifold-projected direction and AdvBench JSR. Does not test adding the direction to induce refusals on harmless requests, preservation of general capability under refusal ablation, or whether the unprojected direction alone is sufficient.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
Does not test whether jailbreak attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
The low-dimensional manifold analysis is for overthinking, not for the refusal direction.
Does not measure harmfulness judgments separately from refusal decisions.
No refusal-direction transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages is tested.
No comparison of refusal training methods or timing is tested.
The reasoning-model experiments concern overthinking, not refusal-direction ablation in reasoning models.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Applied manifold steering for refusal-feature ablation, using direction-computation data from [2].
rows.note: The authors state that all responses were manually verified as valid. The reported manifold-steering alpha is not specified in the text.
rows.check: This is the study's own modified method: the diff-in-means direction projected onto a PCA manifold. It is still a single-direction ablation, so it bears on V1, but it is not the original recipe. Its baseline should be the unablated model's JSR, which the text does not state, not the 74% comparator. The α behind the 100% is not stated in the text; the garbled Figure 6 may show it.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct

source_check.problem: Values match the text. Under Eq. 3 (h' = h - alpha r r^T h), alpha=2.0 reflects the component, so it goes beyond the original's alpha=1 projection. The text gives no judge and no AdvBench subset size.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, AdvBench, unprojected diff-in-means direction ablation (baseline [2]) up to α=2.0

relationships.display_finding: Jailbreak success reached only 74% at α=2.0, with further strength increases risking model collapse.

relationships.reason: Ablating one projected refusal direction yields 100% JSR with manually verified valid responses (r1). Capability retention is not measured.
relationships.display_finding: Ablating one projected direction yielded 100% jailbreak success with manually verified valid responses.

labels.condition: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, AdvBench, unprojected diff-in-means direction ablation (baseline [2]) up to alpha=2.0
labels.reason: 74% JSR at alpha=2.0 means about a quarter of prompts are still not jailbroken, so removal is incomplete (r2). The label is right, but the reason's second sentence misattributes. 'Some instances persist unless intervention strength is increased' is the authors' summary of prior studies [2, 45], not their own measurement. Also, alpha=2 is a reflection, beyond the original's alpha=1 ablation.

relation.reason: The study reports its own JSR results for single-direction refusal ablation on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, both original-style (74%) and projected (100%). These bear on V1, even though the section is framed as a transfer demo for the authors' method.

tranche.reason: Section 5.5 applies a modified single-direction method (a diff-in-means direction projected onto a PCA manifold) to refusal and also reports the unprojected original-style direction. The measure is AdvBench JSR, not the original's JailbreakBench refusal/safety scores. T3 would also be defensible, since the model and dataset are new.

source_check.notes: The refusal result is one paragraph (Sec. 5.5) inside an overthinking paper on R1-distilled models. The paper gives no judge, no AdvBench n, no layer and no number of PCs, and no capability measure. The alpha for the 100% result is not stated, and Figure 6 (alpha 0.4-2) is garbled in the text. Under Eq. 3, alpha>1 is a reflection, not pure ablation.

statements.correction: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, AdvBench: manifold-projected direction 100% JSR (alpha not stated in text); unprojected diff-in-means baseline [2] 74% JSR at alpha=2.0.
statements.problem: The numbers and reading are right for this study. Minor: 'Qwen2.5-7B' could be read as the base model. The text uses Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on AdvBench.
